correctness.rationale: For every n=2,...,8, each listed word set is proved correction-capable by exhausting distinct deletion shadows. Certified positive rational feasible LP primal and dual vectors have matching sums 1,2,4,4,8,13,21, so these are exact fractional optima. At n<8 the integer witnesses meet these bounds. At n=8 a 20-word witness and 77 positive-weight pairwise-conflict cliques cover each of 256 source words with total rational weight 482/23<21. Every clique pair, word-coverage inequality, LP constraint, and objective is exactly checked using Fraction, independently rebuilding all deletion shadows by string and bit operations, with no trust placed in solver output. This proves A_2(8)=20, F_2(8)=21, and no earlier fractional gap in the complete defined domain n>=2. Actual packaged verifier prints VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: Published full-text comparison was by implication. Schoeny et al. define precisely the same exact-burst channel and give a general upper bound that evaluates to 124/5 (integer bound 24) at n=8,b=2, not 20; neither the exact n=8 optimum nor the first fractional-relaxation gap is reported in inspected sections. Ye and Ge give asymptotic construction bounds for a more demanding substring-edit and (<=t)-burst channel, not a length-eight exact cardinality or shadow-LP integrality result. Searches of prior indexed scientific records showed distinct deletion/edit/list channels and no implication of the new finite theorem. Missing primary access to Levenshtein 1967 and imperfect bibliographic indexing retain historical-priority risk; absence of a hit is not asserted as a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The optimum A_2(n) is a natural fundamental code-size invariant of the exact two-adjacent-deletion channel. The cutoff n=8 is not selected solely as a record increment: exhaustive exact rational certificates establish it is the first length at which the standard deletion-shadow fractional transversal/matching relaxation ceases to determine the integral optimum. The new pairwise-conflict clique-cover witness explicitly bridges 21 to 20, revealing a structural limitation of a core upper-bound method and providing a precise, reproducible finite benchmark for stronger synchronization-code bounds. Neither asymptotic results nor previously known run-count identities answer this exact invariant.
